QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On 2026-11-13, QQQ’s 252-return DFA H=0.455 is below the independent finite-variance reference, 0.5. R²=0.936 describes fit only across scales 8–63. Short/long H=0.393/0.648 means one straight-line exponent fits poorly: possible crossover or transient volatility shift, not one clean scaling law. Magnitude DFA-1 H=0.759 suggests stronger volatility clustering than signed returns near 0.5, not tradable predictability.

H fell from 0.520 on 2026-11-06. One/five-observation changes are −0.024/−0.065. Its prior-only 30-observation standardized deviation is −1.33; with overlapping windows, this is not a significance test.

Hill alpha rose from 3.300 on 2026-11-06 to 3.380 on November 11–13. Its 1,000-return (~four-year) window uses k=100 and x_min=0.02018 absolute log-return units. Conditional on a suitable tail model, lower/higher alpha means heavier/thinner fitted tails. SE=alpha/√k=0.338 is an idealized i.i.d. reference that understates dependent-return uncertainty. Plateaus are normal when new returns miss the top k; they do not mean markets are static. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

NVDA.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
NVDA’s 252-return DFA H=0.471 is near, but below, the independent finite-variance reference 0.5. R²=0.963 measures fit only across scales 8–63. Short/long H=0.430/0.636 diverge: one straight-line exponent fits poorly, possibly reflecting crossover or transient volatility shifts, not one clean scaling law. DFA-1 of magnitudes, h_abs=0.644, suggests stronger volatility clustering than signed-return persistence, not tradable predictability.

H rose 0.0012/0.0343 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-only 30-observation standardized deviation is +2.15; overlapping windows prevent significance testing. From 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-13, H rose 0.436→0.471; Hill alpha moved 2.926→2.910.

Hill uses 1,000 returns (~4 years), k=99, x_min=0.04449 absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha means heavier/thinner fitted tails, conditional on a suitable model. SE=alpha/√k=0.292 assumes independence and understates dependent-return uncertainty. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.339/2.865, not a confidence interval. Alpha was unchanged November 12–13; plateaus are normal when new returns miss the top-k extremes, not evidence of stasis. Window entry/exit and threshold changes can affect steps. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
